details:
Project Details – Mission Trainer

Mission Trainer is an interactive, child-friendly space mission and rocket launch simulation platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its main purpose is to make space science and rocket technology easier to understand through hands-on learning and interactive 3D visualization.

Users can select a launch location, choose a destination such as Earth orbit, the Moon, or Mars, and configure their rockets by adjusting fuel, mass, thrust, power, payload, and budget. They can select different engine types, configure multiple rocket stages, and analyze mission feasibility by comparing available Delta-v with estimated mission requirements. The platform then visualizes the rocket launch and displays the mission outcome.

To connect the project with real-world space science, we integrated NASA GIBS services, using Blue Marble Next Generation for Earth's daytime imagery and VIIRS Black Marble for nighttime lights. We also integrated NASA's EPIC API to retrieve Earth observation metadata. Additionally, the project displays the International Space Station's live position using the third-party WhereTheISS.at API.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js for 3D visualization, along with NASA data services and external APIs. Its creative approach combines rocket configuration, simplified physics-based mission analysis, planetary visualization, and interactive launch experiences in one educational platform.

Mission Trainer helps students and young learners develop scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. It transforms complex space mission concepts into an engaging experience where users can experiment, make decisions, and learn from mission results. The simulation is educational and does not represent a certified real-world rocket launch prediction system.

Our future goal is to improve the simulation and integrate additional verified planetary datasets to create more realistic and educational space exploration experiences.
